sources.citation: Leigh R. Hochberg, Daniel Bacher, Beata Jarosiewicz, Nicolas Y. Masse, John D. Simeral, Joern Vogel, Sami Haddadin, Jie Liu, Sydney S. Cash, Patrick van der Smagt & John P. Donoghue (2012). Reach and grasp by people with tetraplegia using a neurally controlled robotic arm. Nature, 485, 372–375.
sources.notes: Landmark May 16, 2012 Nature clinical study demonstrating 3D robotic arm reach-and-grasp by two brainstem-stroke participants (S3 Cathy Hutchinson at 5 years post-implant, and T2), culminating in S3 independently drinking coffee from a bottle (4 of 6 trials).

sources.citation: Leigh R. Hochberg, Mijail D. Serruya, Gerhard M. Friehs, Jon A. Mukand, Maryam Saleh, Abraham H. Caplan, Almut Branner, David Chen, Richard D. Penn & John P. Donoghue (2006). Neuronal ensemble control of prosthetic devices by a human with tetraplegia. Nature, 442, 164–171.
sources.notes: Foundational 2006 Nature first-in-human BrainGate trial showing 96-channel primary motor cortex cursor and simple gripper control after spinal cord injury.

sources.citation: Jennifer L. Collinger, Brian Wodlinger, John E. Downey, Wei Wang, Elizabeth C. Tyler-Kabara, Douglas J. Weber, Angus J. C. McMorland, Meel Velliste, Michael L. Boninger & Andrew B. Schwartz (2013). High-performance neuroprosthetic control by an individual with tetraplegia. The Lancet, 381(9866), 557–564.
sources.notes: Independent University of Pittsburgh Lancet replication extending intracortical motor cortex decoding to 7-degree-of-freedom anthropometric robotic arm coordination.

sources.citation: Apostolos P. Georgopoulos, Andrew B. Schwartz & Ronald E. Kettner (1986). Neuronal population coding of movement direction. Science, 233(4771), 1416–1419.
sources.notes: Mechanistic mathematical foundation proving ensembles of motor cortex neurons encode 3D reaching direction as a summed population vector.

sources.citation: John D. Simeral, Sung-Phil Kim, Michael J. Black, John P. Donoghue & Leigh R. Hochberg (2011). Neural control of cursor trajectory and click by a human with tetraplegia 1000 days after implant of an intracortical microelectrode array. Journal of Neural Engineering, 8(2), 025027.
sources.notes: Longitudinal durability milestone proving Participant S3's 96-channel silicon array continued decoding accurate point-and-click commands at 1,000 days post-implant.

sources.citation: A. Bolu Ajiboye, Francis R. Willett, Daniel R. Young, William D. Memberg, Brian A. Murphy, Jonathan P. Miller, Benjamin L. Walter, Jennifer A. Sweet, Harry A. Hoyen, Michael W. Keith, P. Hunter Peckham, John D. Simeral, John P. Donoghue, Leigh R. Hochberg & Robert F. Kirsch (2017). Restoration of reaching and grasping movements through brain-controlled muscle stimulation in a person with tetraplegia: a proof-of-concept demonstration. The Lancet, 389(10081), 1821–1830.
sources.notes: BrainGate2 follow-up routing intracortical motor cortex signals directly to functional electrical stimulation of a paralyzed participant's own arm to drink coffee.

sources.citation: Francis R. Willett, Donald T. Avansino, Leigh R. Hochberg, Jaimie M. Henderson & Krishna V. Shenoy (2021). High-performance brain-to-text communication via handwriting. Nature, 593, 249–254.
sources.notes: BrainGate2 handwriting breakthrough decoding attempted pen movements from motor cortex at 90 characters per minute.

sources.citation: Chethan Pandarinath, Paul Nuyujukian, Christine H. Blabe, Brittany L. Sorice, Jaimie M. Henderson, Krishna V. Shenoy & Leigh R. Hochberg (2017). High performance communication by people with paralysis using an intracortical brain-computer interface. eLife, 6, e18554.
sources.notes: Addresses signal instability, daily recalibration overhead, percutaneous pedestal tethering, and decoding drift limits in chronic intracortical arrays.

sources.citation: Nature Video (2012). "Paralysed woman moves robot with her mind - by Nature Video."
sources.notes: Official Nature Video clinical documentary footage of Participant S3 (Cathy Hutchinson) steering the DLR robotic arm to grasp, lift, tilt, and sip from a coffee bottle; analyzed locally in media/M1/ for blocking and prop physics only.

sources.citation: Brown University (2012). "BrainGate robotic arm clinical trial demonstration."
sources.notes: Complementary clinical demonstration reference analyzed locally in media/M2/ for robotic joint articulation and tabletop target geometry; never reused raw.
